newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds end week on high note but look vulnerable.
newsitem.headline: Bunds end week on high note but look vulnerable.

text.p: German Bunds and futures headed into the weekend in good spirits, shored up by upbeat U.S. Treasuries and a slightly stronger mark.

But analysts said that the sprint ahead by June futures on Friday looked a little unstable with volumes thin after Thursday's German holiday and said the market may have to take a step back early next week.

By 1410 GMT, the DTB June futures contract was 28 basis poinst up on the day at 101.99, off its earlier high of 102.11 but maintaining strong gains in a session more or less void of trading incentives.
In the cash market, the 10-year benchmark Bund was offering a 5.733 percent yield at a price of 101.97, while the 10-year yield gap to Treasuries was trading at 104 basis points.
"We saw some decent buying of twos and fives earlier on," said a Frankfurt-based trader. "But a lot of people have stayed at home today and there is not much business going through."
After a very subdued end to this week, Bunds have more to get their teeth into next week.
At home, May cost of living and April wholesale prices data are due early in the week, but the big potential mover will be the May tax revenue estimates for 1997 due on Thursday.

Many analysts say the estimates will reveal a severe shortfall -- maybe as much as 20 billion marks, and say Bunds could come under heavy selling pressure if Finance Minister Theo Waigel does not immediately present proposals aimed at making up the loss.
"The market will need to see some concrete plans pretty quickly," said one.
The Bundesbank's regular fortnightly council meeting on Thursday is very unlikely to lead to any change in rates, with recent data confirming a scene of slow growth and low inflation, analysts said.
